findings.title: Main continues dispatching scan RPCs after the user presses Cancel
findings.scenario: A normal scan is processing multiple announcement windows or provider-limit subdivisions when the user presses Cancel, including while waiting in an optional jitter delay.
findings.root_cause: The main UI aborts its scan controller and runScan terminates the worker, but the main window decorator has no signal/current-context guard and dispatches inner.getLogs after awaited jitter and throughout recursive window processing. runScan checks cancellation only after the whole fetchAnnouncements call returns; no cancellation-aware RPC wrapper intervenes.
findings.impact: Additional outbound scan queries can be dispatched after cancellation, disclosing more scan-range and timing activity to the already selected endpoint and delaying completion until current page work settles. This is a cancellation/privacy-consent boundary defect. It does not establish new recipients, key disclosure, transaction submission, or fund loss.
findings.distinction: The finding concerns requests that start after cancellation. It does not claim that already dispatched request bytes can be recalled.

evidence.detail: Client construction omits the scan signal; Cancel aborts the controller.
Abort handler tears down the worker; cancellation is checked after full adapter fetch completion.
Window options have no signal; jitter resumes into dispatch and recursive/window loops continue without cancellation checks.
Current action signal and scope guard are passed into client construction and scan execution.
Signal/current-context checks guard dispatch and scheduling, including after jitter; indexer transport receives action cancellation.
Both RPC clients are wrapped with cancellation/current-context checks for adapter-internal calls.

findings.remediation: Retain the combined candidate cancellation propagation, per-dispatch current-context checks, and abort-aware RPC wrappers when integrating branches. Ensure future decorators do not perform additional dispatches after their action signal is aborted.

existing_tests.detail: Existing source covers pre-aborted calls, cancellation during head/log responses, provider-limit rejection, and cancellation during jitter.
Existing source covers bootstrap refusal, indexer request cancellation, no following windows, and cancellation during jitter.

findings.validation: Static source and existing test-source review only. No tests, app code, probes, transactions or reproduction executed.

observations.description: Browser fetch transport validates endpoint, limits timeout/body, omits credentials/referrer, refuses redirects, and sanitizes injected errors. Transport-to-fetch cannot recall already-dispatched underlying requests; cancellation suppresses late results as documented.

Range/padded candidate adds explicit cancellation checks; indexer, light and quorum helpers are transitively present but browser callsite reachability remains to be checked before any security finding. No source-level test execution occurred.

Candidate runScan wraps both RPC clients with per-call cancellation/current-context guards (189-214). Main lacks this wrapper and scanPrivacy signal checks. compareProviders has no aggregate secondary request/log budget; candidate window wrapper caps 4096 uncached dispatches per getLogs invocation, not the whole secondary comparison; adapter lane owns availability-hardening observation.

Candidate scanSpam marks the 30-day privacy-set count partial when fewer than the available 30 days were scanned; main checked only the 7-day span. Existing heuristic labels remain approximate; not a new candidate security finding.

Private v5 history binds scope/slot/envelope with HKDF and authenticated encryption, rejects malformed/oversized state, reserves empty contexts, and uses CAS/tombstones. Restored matches have receipt claimed; Scan re-fetches discovered blocks before rebuilding payment classification. Independent storage corruption, write races, and session replacement scenarios are present in read test sources; no runtime result is claimed.

Reviewed Scan/scanPrivacy browser callsites offer RPC or indexer log sources. Light/PIR/quorum source helpers were conservatively read from lexical closure; no browser light-client or PIR runtime activation was established. Nonbrowser net-transport native/proxy/OHTTP implementations remain outside the parent-assigned closure scope.

handoff: No assigned production path+blob remains unread. Candidate test sources for nine files and main counterpart differences are reviewed. Remaining inherited tests and package test/support variants are enumerated in pending_tests (local lane status; root must reconcile other workers).
